findings.message: Assessment blueprint violation: Topic 5.1 has only one restricted-response question (RRQ-01) against the approved blueprint's ">= 2 RRQ per topic" (specs/content/gnas-301/content-spec.md:847-848) and the bank's own front-matter claim (docs/semester-1/gnas-301/unit-05/unit-assessment.mdx:9). Repair: add a second 5.1 RRQ (for example naming the six agents with one target organ each, or walking the emission-to-effect chain) and rebalance within the fixed 10-item bank (5.2/5.3/5.4 currently carry three each).

Unsupported citation: docs/semester-1/gnas-301/unit-05/topic-01.mdx:52-54 attributes "particles small enough to cross into the blood and reach the heart" and "the WHO's heaviest single air-health item" to (WHO, 2024). The cited fact sheet (live fetch 2026-09-24) contains no bloodstream or penetration language and ranks no pollutant; it supports only that fine particulate matter causes cardiovascular and respiratory disease and cancers, and carries the 4.2M premature-death figure. Repair: reword the sentence to what the fact sheet supports, or cite a source that carries the translocation mechanism.

Figure geometry defect: static/img/figures/gnas-301/unit-05/fig-U5-3.svg stage panels overlap (x=26/176/326 at width 178 gives 28px collisions covering both arrows between panels 1-2 and 2-3; the third arrow ends at x=518, 58px short of panel 4 at x=576). The flowchart's connector arrows, which carry its instructional point, are hidden or detached; see renders-20260924T000000Z/figrender-fig-U5-3.png. Repair: re-space the four panels (for example width 160 at x=26/216/406/596) and extend each arrow to meet its target box; mirror the fix into the .ur.svg and both .dark.svg variants.

Coverage matrix mislocations (specs/content/gnas-301/coverage/unit-05.md:18-21 and :28): U5-06's Section says "Multilateral environmental agreements" but the SDGs are taught under "### Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)"; U5-07's topic-04 row says "Multilateral environmental agreements" but environmental law is taught under "### Environmental laws, policies, guidelines and strategies related to public health"; the U5-07/park-park row maps environmental law to topic-02.mdx's fate-of-toxins section, which teaches no environmental law; and the reinforcement row maps U5-06 to teacher-notes misconceptions that cover MEAs, not SDGs. The coverage-matrix-v2 contract requires the Section cell to name the exact heading covering the sub-topic (a human-Gate check, FR-013). Repair: correct the four cells; the park-park row should anchor to the section park-park actually supports or carry the sub-topic it genuinely backs.

Year inconsistency: specs/content/gnas-301/sources/unit-05.md:14 says guardans2013 supports "Stockholm POPs 2004" (entry into force, per the bound excerpt) while the unit prose, fig-U5-7 and RRQ-10 all date the convention 2001 (adoption). Both framings are individually correct; align the sources-list wording (for example "adopted 2001, in force 2004") so a reader checking the citation is not confused.

docs/semester-1/gnas-301/unit-05/topic-04.mdx:76-77 says "this course lives inside half of them" for seven of the seventeen SDGs (about 41 percent). Consider "seven of the seventeen" or "more than a third".
MCQ answer key clusters on option b (six of ten; option d is never correct). Not a rubric violation; consider spreading the key across options in the repair cycle.

RRQ-04 and RRQ-07 are not linked to any concept in specs/content/gnas-301/concepts/unit-05.md (the contract permits "-" but every other item is linked); linking them would complete the traceability the concept graph exists to provide.

Several summative items duplicate formative "Check your understanding" items nearly verbatim (RRQ-03 vs topic-02 CYU-3; RRQ-04 vs topic-02 CYU-4; RRQ-05 vs topic-03 CYU-1; RRQ-06 vs topic-03 CYU-3; RRQ-09 vs topic-04 CYU-2), so part of the bank measures recall of practised items rather than independent mastery. No contract forbids this; consider rewording at least the verbatim cases when the bank is repaired.

U5-06 (SDGs) has no direct MCQ or RRQ item; its only summative presence is ERQ-05's instrument choice. The per-topic floor is met (topic 5.4 carries two MCQs and three RRQs), but the SDG outcome rests on a single integrative item.

Input drift during review: HEAD moved 6e2244e -> 9e72f8c -> 1aebf6a as sibling sessions committed to this shared worktree. Exactly one bound input changed, docs/semester-1/gnas-301/course-overview.mdx (rewritten from a coming-soon placeholder to a full overview in commit a495278); impact on Unit 5 criteria assessed as none (course-level landing page; its Unit 5 summary matches the unit). This report binds the post-drift 103-input manifest; the frozen manifest.json is untouched. Because validation recomputes the manifest, any further bound-input change will invalidate this report.

The parent prompt did not pass an explicit author run identity; author_run_id was derived from the unit-05 authoring commit 60655ce on branch 019-author-gnas-301 ("feat(gnas-301): author Unit 5 (Toxicology Essentials and Environmental Governance)"). Independence is nonetheless established: this reviewer session started after that commit and authored none of the reviewed bytes.

Three cited sources (who-chemical-safety, un-paris, un-sdgs) have committed excerpts under sources/texts/ but are not bound in the G3 manifest because citedKeysFor in scripts/lib/review-evidence.mjs only extracts year-suffixed keys. They were inspected as committed on-disk evidence. This is a tooling-level binding gap, not a content defect.

Plan-versus-delivery divergence on the MEA timeline: the content-spec figure plan (content-spec.md:841-843) lists eight points (including Kyoto 1997 and Rotterdam 1998) and the worked-example plan (content-spec.md:812-814) a different set (Rotterdam, Minamata, Montreal, Paris), while the delivered figure and prose carry six (Stockholm 1972, Basel 1989, Rio 1992, Stockholm POPs 2001, Minamata 2013, Paris 2015). The guide names no specific agreements and the delivered six cover everything the assessment tests, so this is not a coverage failure; record the divergence or align the plan.
